suite.description: Multi-device identity vectors (IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §12.2 ID-01 to ID-04): Device Certificates, certificate chains, DEVICE_GRANT and DEVICE_REVOKE with the rules they change, Genesis field 5, transfer commit field 2, and the Data Units, Key Packages, Snapshots and reads they authorize.

conventions.labels: Principals, certificates and Resources are named by fixture labels; fixtures.certificates and the principal_* cases give their bytes.
conventions.context: A Control Record case is proposed on the head reached by replaying, in order, context.records, the records of context.record_set (fixtures.record_sets), when present, and context.records_after_set; context.head_record_id and context.head_control_seq give that head, and context.head names the case that carries it unless it is the last record of a record set. Data Plane objects and reads use context.latest as the receiver's latest Control state.
conventions.variants: A vector of IDENTITY-PROFILE-01 §12.2 with several outcomes is split into cases <vector>.<variant>; the case without a suffix carries the outcome the specification names.
conventions.post_state: For an accepted record, expected.post_state lists the derived state of LFCP-WIRE-01 §79 after it: roles, devices (with activity, suspension and data/read), revoked, the roots with standing, issuer_root for a grant and exposing for a DEVICE_REVOKE.
conventions.rule: Every validation case names in `rule` the section and the rule that decide it; for a rejection, the first failing class of LFCP-WIRE-01 §62.

suite.warning: All private keys, DEKs and derived keys in this suite are public test fixtures. They MUST NOT be used in production or as production defaults.

conformance.validation: An implementation MUST reach every expected validity and, on rejection, report the expected error code; for an accepted record it MUST derive the listed post-state facts.
conformance.bytes: The same inputs MUST produce exactly the expected bytes.
conformance.diagnostics: Within one wire code, implementation diagnostics are not compared.
